To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the Hong Kong Court has come to play a pivotal role in the governance of Hong Kong; 2) this role is the consequence of the Court's successful development of constitutional common law; 3) the Court has developed constitutional common law in ways that are politically realistic; and 4) the Court's constitutional common law has been politically realistic because of the high transaction costs of political decision making in post-1997 Hong Kong.
the Hong Kong judiciary has come to play a pivotal role in shaping the constitutional common law of Hong Kong under Chinese sovereignty.
the Hong Kong Court has developed a sophisticated judicial gloss to the Basic Law in a manner unforeseen by the National People's Congress.

the following question: how can the judiciary in an authoritarian regime, where the legislature and the executive are dominated by a single political party and the judiciary is not formally independent, play a role in the protection of rights and the promotion of the rule of law?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Court's constitutional common law is a product of the political transaction costs that have been created by the resumption of China's sovereignty.
the Hong Kong Court has become the most important political actor in Hong Kong.
the Hong Kong Court is a political actor in the sense that it is capable of influencing the political process, and it has been doing so in a significant and consequential way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Hong Kong Court is able to develop its own constitutional common law in a way that is not only politically feasible but also consistent with the Basic Law.
constitutional common law in the Hong Kong Court has become the most effective mechanism to manage the political costs of the resumption of sovereignty.

the Court has developed a distinctive constitutional common law, which is not merely a copy of British common law but rather is a new hybrid that has evolved to meet the needs of Hong Kong's unique political circumstances.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Hong Kong Court's judicial glossing of the Basic Law is not only a response to political transaction costs, but also a form of political transaction cost creation in itself.
constitutional common law is not a mere by-product of the Court's judicial craftiness.
constitutional common law in the Hong Kong context is a product of the political environment in the city, which is in turn shaped by the Chinese state's own political and economic calculations.
